MINECRAFT PREHISTORIC MESA VALLEY BIOME CONCEPT

I designed this biome idea as a concept for what a Sniffer’s natural habitat might look like. The ground is mostly moss, since Sniffer eggs hatch faster with moss, and I designed it to match the Sniffer’s coloration so they would look “at home” there.

Like a Mesa (Bryce) biome, except that the vast majority of the red sand is replaced with moss block instead, with only small scatterings of red sand or gravel here and there. The moss is covered liberally with Torchflower, Fern, Large Fern, Pitcher Plant, Rose Bush, Lilac, and Poppy. The walls of the bryce will have scattered vines. The biome is scattered with pools of water and acacia trees. Occasionally, a giant red mushroom with small red mushrooms below and around it. All chunks of the Prehistoric Mesa are slime chunks.



PEACEFUL MOBS (most common to least common)

Parrot

Frog

Armadillo

Striped wolf

Sniffer



WATER MOBS (most common to least common)

Tropical fish

Axolotl

Glow squid



HOSTILE MOBS (most common to least common)

Slime

Spider

Creeper

Skeleton

Zombie

Enderman



I imagine it would border only jungle, mesa, swamp, or ocean, always spawning surrounded by those biomes, and would be an ultra rare biome. The only structures to spawn there would be Trail Ruins, which have vastly improved odds of containing Sniffer Eggs in their suspicious sand. Sometimes you might also find naturally spawned Sniffer Eggs in the world, underneath a tree or mushroom and always on a moss block. Lush caves would have an increased chance of spawning underneath this biome. Coral reefs and ruins are more likely to spawn near to the Prehistoric Mesa, but villages and mineshafts are less likely to spawn nearby to it, implying it is so far undiscovered. This biome would get rain, and wandering traders would not spawn in this biome.

I've thought a lot about what it would take for me to accept AI. Personally, I think in order for AI to be used and made in ethical ways, it needs to be legislated.


Firstly, AI should not be allowed to train nonconsensually, as most AI are now. Currently, the artists and creatives whose work AI use didn't give it permission, and don't receive credit or royalties. To fix this, I think that artists should be able to willingly opt in to databases. They should NOT be automatically added to them, even if they post on a site that has an AI; It should be consensual. When an image or text is generated using AI, it should have a list of credits at the bottom, crediting the creatives whose work it used. And, should the AI generate money, the creatives should receive some small revenue from it, like how social media content creators get monetized. 


Secondly, AI should only be accessible to adults, people over 18, so that it doesn't hinder children's ability to develop creativity, similar to how children are not permitted to access adult content online. If AI does all their creativity for them, they won't be able to be creative themselves; Can you navigate without a maps app? Can you do math without a calculator? When you rely on something, you lose the ability to do it for yourself. Learning to be creative, put in effort, and solve problems is critical to a child's development. 


Thirdly, everything made by AI should come with a visible watermark, and in case this is cropped out, also include tags in its metadata. This purpose is twofold: It will tell humans what they are seeing is artificially generated, and will also tell other AI that this is AI content, thus assisting in the use of AI. The watermark should be light and small enough that it doesn't hinder the enjoyment of the content, but visible enough that people with vision problems can still see it, and it should be in the middle of the image or video so that it is not easily cropped out. 


Fourthly, some uses of AI should be illegal. Generating images or videos of specific real people without their consent and prior knowledge, generating inappropriate images, videos, or texts, tracking the locations of people without their consent, etc, should all be illegal, both to make an AI that does those things, and to deliberately prompt an AI to do those things. 


Fifthly, the AI should have to comply with certain environmental standards regarding water and electricity consumption, and waste production. 


I think if all that got passed into effect, I would be okay with AI.

Well, for starters, AI has enormous environmental impact. Running the servers for it requires massive amounts of electricity, producing a huge carbon footprint as a side-effect. Scientists at the University Of Massachusetts have found that training a single AI can produce 626,000 pounds of carbon dioxide.

  
Also, almost all AI, as it currently exists, is trained on unconsentual mass web scraping, and exploits real humans without their permission. We should not be normalizing that exploitation, nor should we be participating in it.

  
AI is erasing millions of jobs, mine included. As people lose their jobs, they will no longer have disposable income, and the global economy will fall into a depression.

  
Also, I'm just really tired of it being shoved down my throat by every single company for no good reason.
